title: 1999 HMMT February Calculus Problem 4
statement: \(f\) is a continuous real-valued function such that \(f(x+y)=f(x) f(y)\) for all real \(x, y\). If \(f(2)=5\), find \(f(5)\).

solutions.text: More generally, since \(f(n x)=f(x)^{n}\) for all integers \(n, f(1)=c=f(1 / n)^{n}\) for some constant \(c\) and all integers \(n\). Thus \(f(k / n)=f(1 / n)^{k}=f(1)^{k / n}=c^{k / n}\) for all rational numbers \(k / n\). By continuity, it follows that \(f(x)=c^{x}\) for all real numbers \(x\). Since \(f(2)=5, c=\sqrt{5}\), so \(f(5)=\mathbf{2 5} \sqrt{\mathbf{5}}\).
